subject: history
title: War, Welfare State and Immigration 1939-1979
welcome_lead: From the Blitz to the Winter of Discontent: the rise of the welfare state and the post-war consensus.
meta_desc: Edexcel A-Level adventure on WWII, the Beveridge Report 1942, NHS 1948, immigration and the post-war consensus.
final_note: You can assess the achievements and tensions of the post-war settlement.

concepts.def: Published 1 December 1942; identified the Five Giants (Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor, Idleness) and proposed comprehensive social insurance.
Attlee's landslide victory (5 July 1945) delivered nationalisation and the welfare state; ousted in October 1951.
Established by Bevan's 1946 Act; opened on 5 July 1948, providing care free at the point of use.
Granted CUKC status to Commonwealth citizens; underpinned the SS Empire Windrush (22 June 1948) and post-war immigration.
Bipartisan acceptance of full employment, the mixed economy, the welfare state and conciliation of trade unions, c.1945-79.
Wave of public-sector strikes against Labour's 5% pay policy, contributing to Callaghan's defeat in May 1979.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Blitz killed about 43,000 British civilians; conscription, rationing and women's mobilisation reshaped society. The Beveridge Report (1942) sold 600,000 copies. Labour's 1945 manifesto Let Us Face the Future won 393 seats. Nationalisation followed: Bank of England (1946), coal (1947), railways (1948), iron and steel (1949). The NHS opened on 5 July 1948.

The Conservatives (1951-64) under Churchill, Eden, Macmillan and Home presided over 'never had it so good' (1957). Suez (1956) shattered imperial pretensions. The SS Empire Windrush (June 1948) and Commonwealth migration met racism (Notting Hill 1958). The Commonwealth Immigrants Acts (1962, 1968) and the 1968 Race Relations Act framed a restrictive but anti-discriminatory regime; Powell's 'Rivers of Blood' speech (April 1968) shocked.

Heath's U-turn (1972), the three-day week (January-March 1974) and the IMF crisis (September 1976) revealed strain. Race Relations Acts (1976) and Equal Pay (1970) reformed work. The Winter of Discontent (1978-79), with refuse and gravedigger strikes, prepared the ground for Thatcher's May 1979 victory.
